newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Woodside sees Cossack output back up.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Woodside sees Cossack output back up.

text.p: Woodside Petroleum Ltd expects to lift Cossack production next month after the completion of repair and maintenance work on its Cossack Pioneer crude oil facility within the next few days, a spokesman said on Thursday.

Work at the facility, which pumps crude oil and gas from the Wanaea and Cossack fields in the North West Shelf, has forced Woodside to cut production to about half design capacity since October 15, spokesman Geoff Wedgwood told Reuters.
Production is running at around 50,000 to 60,000 barrels per day (bpd), he said. Full design capacity is about 115,000 bpd.
"The (repair and maintenance) programme is due to be finished in the next few days. I can't give you an exact date," Wedgwood said.
"It's been a fairly major maintenance and it (production) will build up steadily over the next couple of weeks to normal production," he added. He declined to quantify normal output.
Cossack Pioneer has been plagued by weather-related and technical problems since it was commissioned in November last year. Normal production is reported to be around 90,000 bpd.

Equal partners in the North West Shelf project are Woodside, Japan Australia LNG (MiMi) Pty Ltd and units of The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd, The British Petroleum Co Plc, Chevron Corp and Royal Dutch/Shell Group.
